title: Hazardous Waste Treatment: Technologies, Impacts, and Future Perspectives
content: Hazardous waste management is a major environmental and public health challenge owing to the complexity, toxicity, and volume of waste generated worldwide. Although numerous studies have addressed specific waste streams, treatment technologies, or regulatory aspects, comprehensive assessments integrating regulatory frameworks, waste classification, treatment technologies, operational experience, and emerging energy-system opportunities remain limited. This review provides a multidisciplinary assessment of hazardous waste management, with particular emphasis on the European context. The review combines a bibliometric analysis with a critical evaluation of hazardous waste classification methodologies, generation trends, applicable legislation, conventional and emerging thermal treatment technologies, and documented industrial-scale treatment facilities. Particular attention is given to plasma gasification, including its operating principles, technical advantages, current implementation status, and the lessons learned from European industrial experience. The bibliometric analysis reveals a marked increase in scientific interest, reflecting the growing importance of hazardous waste management within environmental protection and the energy transition. While incineration remains the dominant industrial technology because of its maturity and operational reliability, plasma gasification demonstrates considerable potential for achieving high destruction efficiencies, waste volume reduction, material recovery, and energy recovery. However, its large-scale deployment remains constrained by high capital costs, electricity consumption, and limited industrial experience. This review further identifies an emerging opportunity for the integration of plasma gasification with renewable electricity systems. The increasing availability of surplus renewable electricity, associated with periods of low or negative electricity prices, could substantially improve the economic viability of this energy-intensive technology while contributing to renewable energy integration, grid flexibility, and decarbonization objectives. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological innovation, regulatory development, and energy-system transformation to support more sustainable and resource-efficient hazardous waste management.
